sections.heading: Planned before the panels are made
paragraphs: A hand-painted or panoramic paper is a composition, not a repeating pattern. The panels are made to the elevations, so the plan comes before production: each wall is drawn with its finished width and height and the position of every door, window, socket, radiator, cornice and piece of joinery, and the focal point is agreed. That is often the bed, the chimneypiece or the dining table rather than the middle of the wall.

We measure on site, take out the openings and give the supplier the finished dimensions of the wall that will actually be hung. If the room is still being built or re-plastered, bring the installer and the maker in before the dimensions go to production: skirting height, cornice depth and a new lining all change the finished wall. The [scenic set-out guide](/advice/hand-painted-murals-set-out/) explains each step.

sections.heading: The sequence is the artwork
paragraphs: Scenic papers arrive as numbered panels, hung in the supplied order. On a continuous wall the sequence is not changed to move a motif; only a break in the wall, such as a door or a window, gives the chance to alter it. The delivered panels are checked dry against the maker's layout before any paste and before anything is cut, while a sequence or sizing problem is still easy to resolve. Our [set-out and pattern matching guide](/advice/set-out-and-pattern-matching/) covers the wider set-out.

A hand-painted set cannot be stretched to fit. Its panels are made at a fixed width, and forcing a pasted panel to close a gap stretches it and leads to shrinkage as it dries. Where a door, a window or a corner takes part of the picture, we agree where the loss is least painful: behind a door that stands open, above a window, or in a corner that furniture hides.

sections.heading: The wall beneath a scenic paper
paragraphs: A scenic paper is usually smooth and lit from the side, so the wall has to be sound and true. Some papers are hung over a lining and some are specified without one; de Gournay's instructions, for example, ask for every wall to be lined with plain white lining paper. Where a lining is used, its joints never coincide with the joints of the panels, and it is dry before the panels go on.

New plaster and very absorbent walls are sized as the maker's instruction says, never sealed with neat PVA. Filling, lining and drying time are planned into the programme rather than discovered on the day the panels arrive. The [wall preparation guide](/advice/wall-preparation/) sets out what is checked.

sections.heading: Scenic and chinoiserie papers on the record
paragraphs: At [Brown's Hotel, Mayfair](/projects/browns-hotel-mayfair/), where we were main decorating contractor from 2022 to 2024, the scheme includes scenic and chinoiserie wallcoverings, among them Lewis & Wood's Adam's Eden, designed by Adam Calkin. At a [tea house in West London](/projects/tea-house-jaillon-studio/) designed by Jaillon Studio, the garden room is a panoramic scenic paper of a swan lake and flowering hydrangeas, hung for the reopening in 2021.

Beyond the published case studies, we have installed de Gournay and Fromental papers, including a large volume of Fromental at Four Seasons Ten Trinity Square, and de Gournay in a private residence in London in 2018.

sections.heading: Existing and historic papers
paragraphs: For a paper hung by others, send overall and close-up photographs, the product and batch if known, when the problem appeared and any recent changes, and we will say whether a repair is possible. Marks, flaking or water damage on a hand-painted paper need a paper conservator. We can help find the right person, but we will not experiment on a hand-painted panel.
Our twelve-month workmanship guarantee covers our own installations; it does not transfer to an existing hang by another installer.

sections.heading: What the quotation includes
paragraphs: There is no flat rate per roll, and a roll count will not price a scenic paper. The quotation comes from a site survey or from drawings, and reflects the elevations and panel layout, the state of the walls and any lining, access and protection. Preparation is described separately, with what is included and what depends on inspection. The [installation cost guide](/advice/installation-cost/) explains each item.

We focus on whole residences and hotel packages, and will take on one- or two-room commissions. The minimum installation commission is one room. The [hand-painted papers](/materials/hand-painted/) material page describes what the family needs.

sections.heading: Why the panels differ
paragraphs: Grasscloth is woven from natural fibres, such as sisal, raffia, arrowroot and jute, dyed and laid on a paper backing. Dye takes unevenly on natural fibre, so colour shifts along a roll and between rolls, and once hung each drop reads as a panel with its own tone. Light crossing the wall exaggerates the difference. That is the reason to look at a whole installed wall, not only a sample, before committing a room to it.
Printed and vinyl imitations remove the variation. If a uniform wall is what you want, compare one; the [choosing guide](/advice/choosing-wallcoverings/) covers that decision.

sections.heading: What is normal, and what is a fault
paragraphs: Normal: a visible seam line, a step in tone between neighbouring drops, and a slightly different texture from one panel to the next.

Not normal, and never excused by shading: an open joint, a lifted seam, a dark line or dull patch from adhesive or water on the face, a shiny line where a seam roller has crushed the fibre, drops from two batches on one wall, a narrow sliver at the end of a wall that could have been balanced, or a crease, bubble or tear. Those are installation or handling problems, to be reported rather than lived with. The [grasscloth guide](/advice/grasscloth-seams-and-variation/) explains the difference in detail.

sections.heading: Set-out and shading
paragraphs: Seams land where the wall widths, doors and windows put them, so on a prominent wall the set-out usually starts from the visual centre, the chimney breast or the bed wall, and the end panels are balanced so that neither is a sliver. The direction of the weave is agreed before the first length is cut. Our [set-out and pattern matching guide](/advice/set-out-and-pattern-matching/) explains how a room is set out.

The cut drops are shaded dry, one wall at a time; we hang three and stop to look. Whether alternate drops are reversed is decided by the product's own instruction and a trial on the wall, never by habit. The face is kept free of adhesive and smoothed with a plastic smoother, not a seam roller.

sections.heading: One batch to a room
paragraphs: Variation between batches is larger than variation within one. The whole room is ordered, with a spare, from one batch number, and lengths from the same roll are kept together on the same wall where the room allows. Quantities allow for that, and for the fact that offcuts rarely blend; the [quantities guide](/advice/quantities/) explains why drops, not square metres, decide the order.

sections.heading: Phillip Jeffries and natural weaves on the record
paragraphs: At [Four Seasons Hotel London at Ten Trinity Square](/projects/four-seasons-ten-trinity-square/) we hung Phillip Jeffries Tweed and Omexco between 2016 and 2019, and shading on the natural textiles was checked continuously so the walls read as a single surface. At [The Biltmore Mayfair](/projects/biltmore-mayfair/), then the Millennium Hotel, Grosvenor Square, the 2018 guest-room programme of more than 15,000 m² included a Phillip Jeffries schedule.
Naming a maker records an installation, not an endorsement.

sections.heading: Will it suit the room?
paragraphs: Natural grasscloth is a dry-dust surface. Moisture stains it, adhesive on the face marks it, and it is not suited to frequent wiping or splashes. In a busy hall or beside a kitchen, a textured vinyl may be the better answer if cleaning matters more than natural fibre.

The wall beneath needs to be sound, true and evenly porous, and lined where the maker specifies it. A survey decides that before anything is ordered; see [wall preparation](/advice/wall-preparation/) and the [grasscloth and natural weaves](/materials/grasscloth-and-weaves/) material page.

sections.heading: Why silk is unforgiving
paragraphs: Silk has a cloth face with a sheen that changes as you move. It marks quickly: adhesive on the face, or a ridge at a seam, shows in raking light and cannot be wiped away. Its care is the maker's note, usually dry. It is not a corridor vinyl, and it is specified for rooms where light is part of the finish.

sections.heading: The wall decides the finish
paragraphs: A textured grasscloth forgives small undulations that a silk will show. Where the specification includes it, preparation means stripping old paper, sanding with dust extraction, and making good cracks and uneven surfaces before anything decorative goes up. Period walls can take days of filling and sanding before they are true.

Fresh plaster and filler need time to dry, and a moisture reading, not a calendar date, is the proof. Whether the wall is lined is the maker's call; where a lining is used, its joints never coincide with the joints of the silk, and it is dry first. The primer or size is the one the product's instruction names. The [wall preparation guide](/advice/wall-preparation/) covers each check.

sections.heading: Seams, light and set-out
paragraphs: Seams are planned so the light from the windows does not catch a ridge. Pattern is set out from the room's focal points, such as chimneypieces, doorcases and bed walls, so the pattern sits square to the cornice and the joinery. Deliveries are checked against the measure, and batches and shading are managed so that a room reads as one surface.
Silk is hung with clean hands and an adhesive that suits the cloth, and floors, furniture and finished joinery are protected as part of the hang.

sections.heading: Silks and textiles on the record
paragraphs: At [Four Seasons Hotel London at Ten Trinity Square](/projects/four-seasons-ten-trinity-square/), the hotel wallcoverings of 2019, about 5,000 m², included Fromental silks, alongside Dedar, Vescom, Tektura and Muraspec. At [Raffles London at The OWO](/projects/raffles-london-the-owo/), selected suites have Vescom Alcantara.
Before a silk is ordered, see the sample in the room's own light and confirm the preparation and care it needs; the [silk and textiles](/materials/silk-and-textiles/) material page has the checklist.

sections.heading: What the quotation includes
paragraphs: There is no flat rate per roll. The quotation comes from a site survey or from drawings, and reflects the measured area after openings are taken off, the pattern repeat and the wastage it creates, the state of the walls, lining where it is specified, and access and protection. The [installation cost guide](/advice/installation-cost/) explains each item. We focus on whole residences and hotel packages, and will take on one- or two-room commissions. The minimum installation commission is one room.

sections.heading: Measured to the wall that will be hung
paragraphs: A bespoke mural is printed or painted to the dimensions you supply, so we measure on site, take out the openings and give the supplier the finished dimensions of the wall that will actually be hung. For [Lee Broom's Shoreditch showroom](/projects/calico-lee-broom-overture/), we surveyed in July 2025 for Calico Wallpaper's panel layout and installed on 9 September 2025. At [Heathrow Terminal 4](/projects/heathrow-terminal-4-calico/), Calico's painted landscape was printed to the store's exact wall sizes and wrapped continuously around the corners.

Bring the installer in before the dimensions go to production. A digital print can sometimes be adjusted in the file before printing; a hand-made set cannot be stretched once it exists. The [scenic set-out guide](/advice/hand-painted-murals-set-out/) explains why.

sections.heading: A picture, not a pattern
paragraphs: A mural is one image cut into drops or panels, and each piece has its own place in the picture. Panels are checked against the supplier's layout before hanging, then hung in sequence and matched across every joint. At the [Everyman cinema in Liverpool](/projects/everyman-liverpool/), Muraspec's extra-wide film and music prints were hung as single pictures from floor to ceiling, from the top of the wall down. At Heathrow the horizon had to run level and unbroken across each join and around every corner.

A gradient has no pattern to hide a join: at the [SCP showroom in Pimlico](/projects/scp-showroom-pimlico/) the blue mural was hung in order and butted exactly, so the fade lined up from panel to panel. Wide vinyl can be overlapped and cut through both layers at once, as at [Oxygen Freejumping, The O2](/projects/oxygen-freejumping-the-o2/), so fine lines run unbroken across the joint.

sections.heading: Preparing the wall
paragraphs: A large print shows every bump beneath it. At Everyman the walls were prepared and lined before the murals went up, with scaffold towers and platforms for the tallest walls. Some murals are specified with a lining paper and some without; we follow the specification, and we say at the survey if the wall needs work first.

sections.heading: Fixed dates and live venues
paragraphs: Event murals are hung to a date that does not move. For Ahluwalia and Calico Wallpaper, the [Estuary mural at Rosewood London](/projects/calico-ahluwalia-estuary-rosewood/) was installed in a single day, on 18 September 2026, the day before the show. At Heathrow, the mural was hung overnight on 24–25 September 2018 in a live terminal, by vetted operatives with airside passes, and the finished walls were photographed between 02:30 and 03:42.
At Everyman, the installation ran from October to December 2018, in the weeks before the cinema opened on 18 December.

sections.heading: Murals on the record
paragraphs: Our published murals include Calico Wallpaper's Overture for Lee Broom (2025), Estuary for Ahluwalia (2026) and the Heathrow landscape (2018); Muraspec digital prints at Everyman Liverpool and The O2 (2018); the SCP gradient mural (2019); the panoramic scenic paper at a [tea house in West London](/projects/tea-house-jaillon-studio/) for Jaillon Studio (2021); and large-scale mural setting-out at the [Castle of Trematon](/projects/trematon-castle/) between 2019 and 2022.

A roll calculator will not price a mural. The quotation follows the panel count, the sequence, the substrate and the access the wall needs; the [murals](/materials/murals/) material page lists what to confirm before ordering.

fabric-walling.title: Fabric Walling & Textile Wallcovering, London | Mr Wallcover

sections.heading: Paper-backed textiles and other fabrics
paragraphs: Paper-backed textiles are hung like a wallcovering. Other fabrics have their own method, and we follow the maker's instruction and the designer's specification. Wider goods need more hands and careful handling, especially at corners and openings, and that is planned in the scope.
A textile face marks easily: it is hung with clean hands and an adhesive that suits the backing, and adhesive is kept off the face. The set-out is planned so the joins fall where they are least seen.

sections.heading: Edges, joinery and panels
paragraphs: Fabric walling needs care at the edges and wherever it meets joinery, skirtings and reveals. On panelled walls each panel is its own small wall. At [Hilton London Metropole](/projects/hilton-london-metropole/) the wall panels of a large conference room were covered panel by panel, wrapped so the wallcovering runs the same way on every one and the edges meet on a clean line. At [Huntsman, Savile Row](/projects/huntsman-savile-row/), freestanding display boards were covered in the house's printed tweed, with the pattern square on every edge and face.

sections.heading: Textiles on the record
paragraphs: At [Four Seasons Hotel London at Ten Trinity Square](/projects/four-seasons-ten-trinity-square/), the wallcoverings included Phillip Jeffries Tweed, Fromental silks and Dedar. At [Raffles London at The OWO](/projects/raffles-london-the-owo/), selected suites have Vescom Alcantara. Naming a maker records an installation, not an endorsement.

sections.heading: Preparation and light
paragraphs: A textile wall shows what is beneath it in side light, so the wall is made sound, dry and true first, and lined where the maker requires it. Care follows the maker's note, usually dry. The [wall preparation guide](/advice/wall-preparation/) and the [silk and textiles](/materials/silk-and-textiles/) material page explain what is checked.

sections.heading: What the quotation includes
paragraphs: The quotation comes from a site survey or from drawings: the measured area, the width of the goods and the wastage they create, the state of the walls, lining where specified, and access and protection. Aftercare is included, with a return visit once the room has settled and a twelve-month guarantee on the workmanship. The [installation cost guide](/advice/installation-cost/) explains each item.

sections.heading: Installed as the system was specified
paragraphs: An acoustic wallcovering is a textured face over an acoustic construction, or an acoustic panel. Its performance belongs to the system, so adhesive, trimming, edges and cuts follow the instruction for that system, and nothing is changed on site that would alter what was specified.
We do not claim that a decorative finish carries an acoustic rating. A decorative texture is not evidence of acoustic performance.

sections.heading: Evidence and handover
paragraphs: Acoustic performance, like fire and environmental performance, is evidenced by the exact product's own documents, accepted by the responsible project professional. Before ordering, obtain the system data and the installation detail, and confirm the project's acceptance. The handover then records the installed product, colourway and batch room by room, with spare material from the same batch. The [designer specification checklist](/advice/designer-specification-checklist/) lists the fields.

sections.heading: Junctions with other finishes
paragraphs: Acoustic finishes often sit beside other wallcoverings and joinery in the same room, so the set-out and every junction are planned at the survey, with trims and edges agreed before the run starts. In a hotel or office that stays open, the work is contained and moves around the building's use, as on our [hotel programmes](/services/hotel-wallcovering-installation/).

sections.heading: Acoustic work on the record
paragraphs: At [an office in Holborn](/projects/#record-an-office-in-holborn-2020) in 2020: sound-absorbent acoustic felt wallcovering on a boardroom wall, wrapped around free-standing columns and on a feature wall in an open-plan office.

sections.heading: What the quotation includes
paragraphs: The quotation comes from a site survey or from drawings, and reflects the measured area, the system's own installation requirements, the state of the walls, and access and protection. Aftercare and the twelve-month workmanship guarantee apply as with any other material. The [acoustic wallcoverings](/materials/acoustic/) material page and the [developer package guide](/advice/developer-wallcovering-package/) cover the specification side.

sections.heading: Architectural film on the record
paragraphs: At [Heythrop Park](/projects/#record-heythrop-park-2022), Enstone, Oxfordshire, in 2022, we refinished the passenger lift car interiors in architectural film: a linen texture above dark wood grain, fitted at night over several visits.

sections.heading: Film or wallcovering on joinery
paragraphs: Film suits hard-wearing, wipe-clean surfaces in busy areas: hotel bedroom doors, wardrobes, lifts and counters. Wallcovering suits pattern, texture and continuity with the walls, as at [Raffles London at The OWO](/projects/raffles-london-the-owo/), where the wallcovering continued from the walls onto parts of the joinery. Where both could work, we sample both in the room.

sections.heading: How a wrapping package runs
paragraphs: The survey checks every surface: sound, smooth and non-porous faces take film, while flaking, damp or heavily textured ones need work first. A sample on a real door or panel is approved in the room's own light before the run is ordered. Surfaces are then cleaned, keyed, filled and primed to the film maker's instruction, and edges, corners and returns are finished as agreed on the sample.

Risk assessments and method statements (RAMS) are issued for every package, and Dorin Burcus personally supervises the site. In a hotel or office that stays open, the work goes room by room or floor by floor, and each area is handed back as it is finished. Aftercare is part of the commission: a return visit about four to six weeks after completion and a twelve-month workmanship guarantee.

sections.heading: Window film on the record
paragraphs: At [Hyde London City](/projects/old-bailey-hotel/) (the Old Bailey Hotel), Solar Screen window film was fitted to the glazing as part of our full decorating package, alongside paint and specialist wallcoverings, in the Grade II-listed building that opened as a hotel on 2 September 2024.

sections.heading: How a window film job runs
paragraphs: The survey looks at the glass, the frame, the orientation and what the room needs, and the film maker's guidance decides what can be applied to that glazing. On the day, the glass is cleaned, the film is cut to the visible pane and squeegeed out, and the edges are finished to the frame. A slight haze while the adhesive cures is normal, and we explain what to expect.

Risk assessments and method statements (RAMS) are issued for every package, and Dorin Burcus personally supervises the site. Film can be part of a wider decorating commission, as at Hyde London City, or a job on its own.

sections.heading: Doors papered in
paragraphs: A flush door in a papered wall can disappear when the pattern is carried across its face and trimmed to its edges. At the [SCP showroom in Pimlico](/projects/scp-showroom-pimlico/), a full-height flush door was papered in with the gilded marbled wallcovering so that it almost vanishes into the marbling. At [Lee Broom's Shoreditch showroom](/projects/calico-lee-broom-overture/), Calico Wallpaper's Overture, a trompe-l'oeil theatre curtain, runs straight across a flush door in the back wall, the pattern carried over the door so that it disappears into the drape. The [set-out and pattern matching guide](/advice/set-out-and-pattern-matching/) explains how a pattern is kept continuous across a break like this.

sections.heading: Panels wrapped one by one
paragraphs: On panelled walls each panel is its own small wall. At [Hilton London Metropole](/projects/hilton-london-metropole/), the wall panels of a large conference room were covered in Vescom panel by panel, each wrapped so the wallcovering runs the same way on every one and the edges meet on a clean line, because the room is seen all at once from the doors. At [Huntsman, Savile Row](/projects/huntsman-savile-row/), freestanding display boards were covered in the house's bespoke tweed print: four edges and two faces on each board, with the pattern square on every one.

At [Jumeirah Carlton Tower](/projects/jumeirah-carlton-tower/), where we installed wallcoverings for eight months during the renovation, Jumeirah describes the bedrooms as light oak panelling with textured wallcoverings set into the panels. Inset work leaves nowhere to hide: every edge meets a moulding or a frame.

sections.heading: Edges that stay true
paragraphs: Where an edge will not come true, we stop asking the paper to make it. In [a prime residence in central London](/projects/imperfect-arches-external-corner-trim/), an arch that was not true was given a specialist external-corner profile, bent to the curve and fixed, with the paper scribed into its return, so the edge reads as one crisp line and is protected from wear. At the [Mercedes-AMG showroom](/projects/mercedes-amg-showroom-london/), black matt Muraspec was cut to meet narrow brushed stainless-steel trims at the doors and above the skirtings on one continuous line.

sections.heading: Survey, scaffold and sequence
paragraphs: An exterior starts with a survey that decides access, repairs and the programme, and the order of elevations. On both exteriors published here, we supplied and managed the scaffold for the front and the rear, including the strike. Repairs come before paint: cracks in cornices, pediments and porticos are made good, and stucco and render repaired, before the masonry is painted.

sections.heading: Two exteriors on the record
paragraphs: At St George's Square, Pimlico, the survey was in June 2024 and the works ran from July to November 2024; the scaffold was struck in late November. Repairs took in the cornice, the pediment, the portico and the parapet, and the masonry and render were painted in a Dulux Trade system, with sills, entrance joinery, columns, balustrade and railings finished with the elevation.

At Inverness Terrace, Bayswater, a Victorian stucco terrace of flats, the main run was June to September 2018, busiest in September, with return visits in October and December. Stucco and render were repaired, including cornices, ornamental capitals and architraves, and the balconies, the portico, the windows and the rear brickwork were in the same scope. The finished scheme is a Dulux Trade off-white.

sections.heading: Lime and heritage finishes
paragraphs: Limewash is applied by Mr Wallcover's own team. Lime render can be arranged through trusted specialist partners. On a listed building we follow the specification and whatever the consents for the building allow.
